summary: The note argues that esports is becoming an established part of education, through scholastic leagues like NASEF, school arenas, clubs, and university programs. It covers the social, academic and life-skill benefits cited by educators and researchers, the range of esports careers, and upcoming events such as the Global Esports Education Summit on December 5, 2023.
one_line: Esports is moving into schools via leagues, arenas, clubs and degree programs, bringing social, academic and career benefits to students.
key_facts: The note is dated 10th November 2023 and describes esports as a multi-billiondollar entertainment industry and an emerging pillar in scholastic development.
The National Scholastic Esports Federation (NASEF) operates across the United States and offers students structured leagues.
Dr. Mark Benson, a leading advocate for scholastic esports, says esports in schools offer cognitive and social benefits, from strategic thinking to team-building.
Teams form around games such as 'League of Legends', 'Overwatch', and 'Rocket League'.
On September 15, 2023, Lincoln High School won the state championship, credited to exceptional teamwork.
Sarah Jennings, team captain at Lincoln High, says she used to be shy but the esports team helped her open up and trust her team.
Professor James Clay of UCLA found that students in esports programs tend to improve academic performance, noting a positive correlation between competitive gaming skills and classroom learning.
On October 22, 2023, Summit Academy announced a state-of-theart esports arena with high-performance computers, ergonomic gaming stations, and a broadcast production suite.
Thomas Ballard, IT director of Summit Academy, says the facilities give students a learning environment that rivals professional teams.
Esports careers include professional players, coaches, analysts, broadcasters, content creators, marketing, event organization, and technical support.

Rachel Armstrong, director of the esports program at Tech Valley University, says the curriculum is developed with industry experts; local universities offer degrees and certifications in esports management, digital content creation, and game design.
Jack Richards, a high school senior, organized a local tournament that raised funds for children's hospitals.
The Global Esports Education Summit will convene on December 5, 2023, bringing together educators, industry leaders, and students.
Mike Thompson, a guidance counselor, says esports build resilience, adaptability, and a proactive mindset.
